_schema: mchatai-source/sources/_kinds.json (Phase AV.16, 2026-11-10): what kind of thing each source carries, and the words a person uses to ask for it. Compiled into personas/_index.json as `sourceKinds` (kinds, personal, regions) by verbs/build_index.py.
_why: On the iPad, "Get me the current news" searched arXiv, PubMed and Hacker News because every search covered every source. When a sentence uses a kind's words, an open search covers only the sources of that kind; a sentence with none of these words still searches them all.
_personal: A site the person adds (a feed or a front page) is news unless they say otherwise; that is what the sites added so far are.
_regions: A region narrows an open search to the sources of that place plus any that take search words. "national" means the United States for now: the catalog's own news feeds are mostly American and British.

newsFeeds._why: Phase AV.17: the AI News applet's feeds (news/feeds.json, already shipped in that applet) are also agent sources, compiled by verbs/build_index.py. English feeds only; video and Reddit feeds are left out.

outletSearch._why: Phase AV.18: a topic search on Google News comes back from the outlets that cover it (for Seattle real estate: The Seattle Times, Seattle Met, The Stranger). The agent then searches the outlets that answered most, one at a time, with this query, so a place or subject reaches its own sites without a list of them.

recentQuery._why: Phase AV.28: Google News search takes 'when:' inside the query, so a time window asks the feed itself for recent items.

_nameFillers: A source is also named by its title without these words, so "NPR" names NPR News and "BBC" names BBC Top Stories.
_defaultKinds: Phase AV.19: what an open search covers when the sentence asks for no kind. Before this it covered every source in catalog order, so 'look up X' read arXiv first.
_siteFinder: Phase AV.19: an agent made with no sites named offers sites to pick: the subject is searched in these sources, one candidate per site, the web's results first and then the outlets news search answered with. The person ticks the ones to keep. `browse` are searches the person opens and reads themselves under the card; the app never reads those result pages, only the address of a site the person chose to open and add.
_kindsWithNoSource: Phase AV.20: jobs, travel, deals, recipes and events are carried by no source on purpose: a kind nothing carries is the web's (defaultKinds), which joins the search and ranks as if it carried it.

answerShapes._whenNote: Phase AM.5g (2026-11-15): 'when' only as a question about now or later. Bare 'when' gave 'When did the trial that closed Pike Place to cars begin?' the times shape, and the reader told the model 'This page does not list the times asked for' right above the answer (April 2025).

_answerShapes: Phase AV.28 (2026-11-13): a question that asks when, how much or who won wants a page that says it. When the page the agent reads has no match for the shape's pattern, the next results in the list are read instead (up to two), and a long page shows the model the lines that match, each with the lines above it. 'What movies are showing today in Seattle?' read showtimes.com, a list of films with no times, while seattlemovies.org, third in the same list, has every theater's times (simulator flywheel, 11-13). Words are whole words or phrases of the sentence. `ignore`: a matching line that also matches this is not an answer (a time beside a year is an article's timestamp, not a showtime: 'Oct. 24, 2025, 6:30 a.m.' passed for the SIFF Egyptian's showings, 11-13). A time needs am or pm: a bare '2:24' was a trailer's length on a TV series page read for 'movies playing in Ballard tonight' (11-13). Words are phrases where a bare word is also a command: 'Open TouchLanguage' asked for opening times through the bare word 'open' (11-13). `maxLine`: an answer sits on a short line; a match inside a longer one is a paragraph, not an answer (Fandango's only 'times' were promo fine print, 'ends 11:59 PM', in 400-character lines, so its page counted as having showtimes, 11-14).

sharpen.travel: When are you going, and for how long?
sharpen.events: Which day or night works for you?
sharpen.real-estate: What is your budget, and how many bedrooms?
sharpen.jobs: Where are you looking, and is remote OK?

_sharpen: Phase AV.28: a plan that depends on details the person did not give ends with one question. Apple's 3B model did not ask it ('I want to travel to Mexico City, what are some good activities to do?', 11-13), so the app adds the asked kind's question when the reply asks none and the sentence matches no `sharpenUnless` (a date, a month, a budget).
_kindWords_space: Phase AV.28: science no longer claims the bare word 'space': 'How much are tickets to the Space Needle?' searched the science sites and answered with a $110,000 spaceflight prize (simulator, 11-13).
_timeWindows: Phase AV.28 (2026-11-13): words that ask for a time ('tomorrow', 'this weekend', 'latest') are a filter, not search words. 'What is happening in Seattle tomorrow' searched the word 'tomorrow' and found months-old headlines that say it (Summer Fest, the World Cup match). Now the window's words leave the query, a source's own date filter is used where it has one (`search.recent` on the URL, `search.recentQuery` inside the query), and dated items older than `maxAgeDays` are dropped; undated items (most web results) stay. A question that asks for times, prices or a score (an answer shape) wants a fact page, which is often old (a museum's hours page): for it the window's words stay in the query ('movies showing today' finds the day's listings; without 'today' seattlemovies.org dropped out) and the sources' date filters are not used.
